mutations.name: OVER-REACH CONTROL: the walker lowercases EVERY string value, not just recognized `type` spellings — the shape a careless 'just normalize the schema' refactor produces. Note the narrower version of this mutation (widening the key test to include `description`) injects NOTHING, because the allowlist still rejects a prose sentence: the key test and the allowlist are two independent gates and only bypassing both is observable.

mutations.name: SURVIVOR (documented): the depth bound is removed. Harmless in the CURRENT call graph and not guardable without a fixture that is itself the test: reaching it needs a schema nested deeper than 12, and a JSON body that deep has already been parsed by JSON.parse, which enforces its own nesting limit long before this walker runs — so the recursion is bounded by the parser, not by this line. The bound is kept as a local, readable guarantee (the reader should not have to reason about the parser to see the walk terminates), and it mirrors the depth cap in response-store's field walk. Re-run this mutation if the walker is ever fed a schema built in-process rather than parsed from a request body — then the parser's limit no longer applies and this becomes the only bound.
mutations.anchor: if (depth > 12 || node == null || typeof node !== 'object') return node;
mutations.replacement: if (node == null || typeof node !== 'object') return node;
